concept.name: Political Spectrum
concept.description: The left-right political spectrum as a symmetric bipolar scale with a meaningful neutral centre (centrist/moderate). Nine states run from far-left through centre to far-right; nine transitions describe movement along the spectrum, including the semantically distinct act of crossing the centre point itself. Deliberately built against HL-BI rather than the taxonomy's own suggested 'Diagonal' for this shape — see notes.
concept.taxonomy_path: Mental -> Opinion/Belief -> Political orientation (new entry; the existing taxonomy 'Left/right' entry at 13.2 is the unrelated spatial/directional sense)
concept.notes: Built as a deliberate worked example resolving the open HL-BI question flagged in Conceptionary_Aspectual_Template_Selection_Framework.md (2026-08-24) -- Political Spectrum has a genuine, meaningful neutral zero-point (centrist) with two symmetric extremes, exactly HL-BI's signature shape. The transitions ('shifting left', 'leaning further right', 'crossing the centre') read as atelic/incremental (gradual, no absolute finish line) -- supporting ATSF's tentative hypothesis that HL-BI's transitions are a special case of Degree Achievement organised around a meaningful zero, rather than sitting entirely outside the aspectual framework. Also surfaced a separate, larger finding while building this: 32 of 33 entries in GPCV_Master_Concept_Taxonomy_v2.md labelled 'Spectrum around centre' point to 'Diagonal' as the suggested template family -- but Diagonal is a single-direction line with no true return/centre, the opposite shape from what 'spectrum around centre' actually describes. This card was built against HL-BI in spite of that labelling, not in agreement with it. Flagged for a full taxonomy audit, not corrected in bulk here. Colour scheme deliberately avoids real-world political party colours (red/blue), since which party maps to which colour is itself contested and reverses between countries -- used a neutral grayscale instead.

template_selection_flags.reason: See notes -- taxonomy's 'Spectrum around centre' label systematically points to the wrong family across 32 entries
